phases.title: Survival
phases.goal: Greet people, order food, and cover basic needs using the present tense.
can: Pronounce Italian's five clear vowels and double consonants (pizza, nonno)
Use essere and avere in the present (io sono, io ho)
Greet and introduce yourself formally (Lei) and informally (tu)
Count from 0 to 100 and ask basic prices
Order at a bar or restaurant with 'vorrei' and 'per favore'
Ask 'Dov'è...?' and 'Quanto costa?' to get around
phases.daily: 20 min: 10 min vocabulary flashcards (numbers, greetings), 5 min listening to a short dialogue, 5 min saying essere and avere aloud.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.goal: Talk about daily routines and the recent past.
can: Conjugate regular -are, -ere, and -ire verbs in the present
Form the passato prossimo with avere and essere
Choose the right definite and indefinite articles by gender
Make adjectives agree in gender and number (-o/-a/-i/-e)
Use the partitive (del, della, dei) to say 'some'
Describe your family and routine with reflexive verbs (mi sveglio)
phases.daily: 30 min: 10 min new verbs, 10 min writing three sentences about your day, 10 min a graded podcast or video.

phases.title: Core Structures
phases.goal: Narrate in the past and express future plans and polite wishes.
can: Contrast the imperfetto and passato prossimo when telling a story
Use ci and ne correctly (ci vado, ne voglio due)
Form the futuro semplice and the condizionale (partirò, vorrei)
Combine object pronouns (me lo, glielo)
Give commands with the imperativo, informal and formal
Compare things with più/meno...di/che and build superlatives
phases.daily: 40 min: 15 min grammar drills, 15 min reading a short article, 10 min shadowing or speaking practice.

phases.title: Fluency
phases.goal: Handle opinions, hypotheticals, and most everyday conversations with confidence.
can: Use the congiuntivo presente after penso che, spero che, è importante che
Form the trapassato prossimo for the earlier of two past events
Build if-clauses with congiuntivo imperfetto + condizionale (se avessi tempo, verrei)
Express the passive with essere/venire and the si passivante
Link ideas with relative pronouns che and cui
Report speech with the past conditional (ha detto che sarebbe venuto)
phases.daily: 45-60 min: 20 min native content (podcast or series), 20 min conversation with a partner or tutor, 15 min reviewing mistakes.

phases.title: Mastery
phases.goal: Grasp nuance, register, and literary or regional forms with near-native ease.
can: Recognize and read the passato remoto in novels and news
Use the condizionale composto for unrealized past actions (avrei voluto)
Master the full periodo ipotetico, including the impossibility type
Shift smoothly between formal, informal, and idiomatic register
Understand regional accents and common colloquial expressions
Write structured texts with connectors (nonostante, affinché, tuttavia)
phases.daily: 60+ min: immerse through books, film, and news; write a weekly journal entry; discuss abstract topics and get corrections.
